sources.entry: MiroTalk C2C - Real-time cam-2-cam video calls & screen sharing, end-to-end encrypted, to embed in any website with a simple iframe. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: MiroTalk C2C is a self-hosted, open-source WebRTC platform for 1-to-1 peer-to-peer video calls with screen sharing and end-to-end encryption, embeddable in other websites via iframe.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a self-hosted WebRTC cam-to-cam platform for private 1-to-1 peer-to-peer video calls with screen sharing and end-to-end encryption. Calls can be embedded in any website with a simple iframe integration. Users can choose camera background effects (Off, Blur, or Image) in Settings, with images processed locally in the browser using MediaPipe, which is lazy-loaded from jsDelivr and a model loaded from Google Storage. A picture-in-picture camera bubble can be shown over a shared screen in one of four corners, drawn in the browser and sent as a single video stream. Setup is via Node.js (npm install, npm start) or Docker Compose using an official Docker Hub image. Documentation covers self-hosting, integration, direct room join, a REST API, and ngrok.
use_cases: self-hosted private video calls between two people
embedding a video call widget in a website
running a private WebRTC calling server on my own host
adding camera blur or custom background to video calls
how_to_run: Docker alternative: copy .env.template to .env, copy frontend/js/config.template.js to frontend/js/config.js, copy docker-compose.template.yml to docker-compose.yml, then run docker-compose pull and docker-compose up
notable: Embeddable in any website with a simple iframe
Browser-side camera background blur or image replacement, with images not uploaded
Picture-in-picture camera bubble composited over shared screen
Official Docker Hub image plus Node.js setup
Part of the wider MiroTalk suite (SFU, P2P, BRO, C2C, WEB, CME, ADM)
caveats: Camera-while-sharing bubble is desktop browsers only and needs canvas stream capture; falls back to plain screen share otherwise
Background effects require WebGL2 and external hosts (jsDelivr, Google Storage) to be reachable and allowed by any custom CSP
frontend/js/config.js is sent to the browser, so secrets must not be stored there
keywords: run my own video call server
